Gastroenterology · published research

Reflux laryngitis

Summary of the Evidence

Two related publications from one Brazilian research team tested PBM in rats with laryngitis induced by nasogastric intubation. The studies used different red and near-infrared protocols and reported short-term inflammatory and repair outcomes. No human study was identified (Marinho et al. 2013; Marinho et al. 2014).

Human and clinical evidence

No clinical trial has tested PBM for reflux laryngitis in people. The animal model examines tissue inflammation and repair after a defined procedure; it does not measure hoarseness, throat discomfort, cough, swallowing, voice quality, endoscopic healing, or recurrence in patients.

Animal evidence

In the 2013 experiment, combined 780-nm near-infrared and 660-nm red light modulated neutrophil infiltration and mast-cell degranulation and improved granulation tissue and collagen deposition. The combined protocol produced a better collagenization pattern than untreated intubation and the tested 780-nm protocol alone (Marinho et al. 2013).

In the 2014 experiment, 780-nm near-infrared treatment reduced neutrophil influx and improved reparative collagenization after laryngitis was induced by a nasogastric tube (Marinho et al. 2014).

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The 2013 protocol combined 780 nm at 17.5 J/cm² with 660 nm at 10 J/cm². The reported energies were 2.1 J and 1.2 J, with 30 seconds for each wavelength at three laryngeal points over four sessions (Marinho et al. 2013). The 2014 protocol used 780 nm at 105 J/cm² for 180 seconds at three points, also over four sessions (Marinho et al. 2014). These regimens were not compared in a dose-finding study and do not establish an effective dose for the human larynx.

Interpretation

Both reports found favorable inflammatory or repair changes in an induced rat model. The findings support a local biological effect, but do not establish relief of human reflux-laryngitis symptoms or lasting laryngeal healing.

Publications and records

Certainty of evidence (estimate)

Very low for reduced inflammation and improved tissue repair in induced rat laryngitis

Both reports come from one research team and use the same model family (Marinho et al. 2013; Marinho et al. 2014).

Rationale for the certainty assessment

Two related rat studies from one research team found favorable inflammatory and repair changes in a nasogastric-intubation model. The evidence is limited to short-term histology in one model, with no independent research group and no human data on symptoms, voice, or endoscopic healing (Marinho et al. 2013; Marinho et al. 2014).
